review_text: I'm a solo traveler and found Cozumel very easy to navigate. I just rented a scooter and rode around the island. The east side is deserted and beautiful. Roatan was a bit harder to do alone as the taxis are expensive for one person. I ended up joining a group for a snorkeling trip. Costa Maya is impossible to enjoy alone without spending a lot of money on a taxi or a tour. The port area is fine but everything is priced for tourists. I'd recommend Cozumel for anyone who likes to explore independently.

review_text: Roatan ended up being the highlight for us. We booked a small-group snorkeling trip and the water clarity was unreal compared to what we've seen elsewhere. The boat ride was short and smooth, and we had plenty of time in the water without feeling rushed. Costa Maya felt very manufactured in comparison-we walked through the port area and didn't feel compelled to go further, so we headed back early. Cozumel was somewhere in between; we grabbed a taxi downtown and wandered around, which was enjoyable but crowded. Overall, the itinerary felt a bit uneven, but Roatan alone made it worth it.

review_text: I'm a big diver so Roatan was the main event for me. The reef there is in much better shape than Cozumel. We did a two-tank dive and saw a few reef sharks and a massive grouper. The boat pick-up was right near the pier, very efficient. In Cozumel, the current was quite strong the day we were there, so the drift dive was a bit faster than I like. For Costa Maya, I decided to just relax. I walked down to the Malecón in Mahahual and found a small spot with a bucket of beers for twenty bucks. It was a nice break from the ship's prices. If you're a diver, Roatan is a must, but Cozumel is still decent for the convenience.

review_text: We had a mixed experience with the port excursions. In Roatan, we booked a 'semi-sub' tour to see the reef. It was great for my elderly mother who can't snorkel. We saw turtles and rays through the windows. However, the tour started 30 minutes late and we were worried about our afternoon plans. In Costa Maya, we went to the beach at Mahahual. The seaweed was quite bad that day, which isn't anyone's fault, but it made swimming difficult. The local vendors are also very persistent, which got tiring after an hour. Cozumel was our favorite stop. We went to the Mayan Cacao Company. We learned how to make traditional chocolate and the samples were delicious. The facility was clean and the staff were very professional. I think the time spent in Cozumel was just right, but I would have traded some Costa Maya time for more time in Roatan.

review_text: Cozumel was the easiest port to explore on our own, and we spent most of the time just walking around and stopping at small shops near the waterfront. Roatan was more excursion-based for us, and we did a zipline and beach combination that was fun but slightly rushed. Costa Maya didn't offer much for us without an excursion, so we stayed within the port zone. It was clean and safe but didn't feel like we experienced the destination itself. I'd say Cozumel works best for casual exploring while Roatan is better for planned activities.

Just be prepared for a lot of time on a bus.

review_text: Cozumel was fantastic for snorkeling! We headed over to Money Bar. It's an easy taxi ride from the pier and the entry is free if you eat or drink there. The gear rental was cheap and the reef right off the shore is surprisingly healthy. Lots of parrotfish and even saw a small ray. Roatan was also nice, but the pier area is a bit chaotic with everyone trying to sell you tours. We ended up just taking a water taxi to West End which was much more chill than the main cruise beach. Costa Maya was our 'stay on the ship' day. The port area there feels very artificial, like a theme park version of Mexico. We did walk out for half an hour but it was just rows of the same jewelry and souvenir shops you see at every other Caribbean stop. If you don't book a specific excursion to the ruins or a private beach club, there isn't much 'real' culture to see within walking distance of the boat.

Cozumel had the most developed infrastructure, which made it easy to navigate, but also made it feel less unique. I think expectations matter a lot-if you're looking for convenience, Cozumel delivers, but if you want something different, Roatan stands out.

review_text: Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown for me. The port area feels very manufactured and touristy. We took a taxi to Mahahual, which was better, but the vendors there are extremely pushy, making it hard to just relax on the beach. Cozumel was much better organized. We did the underwater oxygen helmets and it was a surreal experience seeing the fish so close without needing a SCUBA certification. Roatan was beautiful but we had a major delay getting off the ship due to local port authorities, which cut our excursion time short by nearly an hour. We still managed to see the monkeys and sloths, but everything felt rushed. I'd recommend this itinerary for the scenery, but be prepared for some logistical headaches at the piers.

review_text: Roatan ended up being my favorite stop, which surprised me. We booked a small group snorkeling trip, and the water clarity was unreal. I've snorkeled before but never saw reefs that vibrant so close to shore. The only downside was how rushed the return felt-we barely had time to dry off before heading back to the ship. In Costa Maya, we tried to explore on our own, but the port area felt very manufactured and crowded with shops. We eventually took a taxi to a quieter beach, which improved the day a lot. Cozumel felt more flexible; we just wandered downtown, grabbed drinks, and people-watched. It wasn't as visually striking as Roatan, but it felt less rushed and easier to navigate.

review_text: The ports were nice but I felt like the excursions were overpriced for what you got. In Roatan, we paid for a 'private beach' that turned out to be packed with people from three different cruise lines. The buffet lunch was cold chicken and rice. Cozumel was better because we just walked to a local pharmacy and then a grocery store to buy real Mexican vanilla and candy. Much better prices than the 'official' shops. Costa Maya was fine, we just sat by the port pool. It's free, but the drinks are expensive. The time in port was enough for us, honestly, we were ready to get back to the AC by 2 PM.

review_text: Loved the port in Costa Maya, specifically the chocolate making demo near the back of the plaza. It's free and very educational. We also took the tram to the local village which was $4. The beach there is narrow but the restaurants have great vibes. Cozumel felt a bit too commercialized this time around. We've been there many times and it seems like the prices for taxis just keep going up. Roatan remains my favorite because of the lush landscape, though the humidity was nearly unbearable the day we visited.

review_text: I've cruised a few times and this itinerary was decent but not perfect. Roatan stood out because we booked a private driver who customized the day-snorkeling, a short hike, and lunch at a local spot. That felt authentic. Costa Maya, on the other hand, felt like it was built purely for cruise traffic. We walked beyond the port and found a quieter beach, but it took effort. Cozumel was predictable but enjoyable. We did a catamaran snorkel, which was fun but definitely crowded. Timing at each port felt slightly uneven, with Costa Maya having more time than we needed and Cozumel not quite enough.

review_text: We had a blast in Cozumel doing the electric bike tour. It takes you along the coast away from the main town and you get to see some of the smaller ruins on the island. It's much cooler than sitting on a bus. Roatan was also great; we did the 'Little French Key' day trip. It was a bit pricey but it was so peaceful and the lunch was delicious-fresh lobster and coconut rice. Costa Maya was the only 'meh' day. We did the Bacalar Lagoon tour, which was a very long drive. The lagoon is stunning, the 'seven colors of blue' are real, but I spent more time on a bus than I did in the water. If you don't mind long travel times, it's worth it, but if you want to relax, maybe pick something closer to the pier. Overall, a great mix of activities across the three stops. I felt like I got a good taste of both Mexico and Honduras.

It was a bit pricey but it was so peaceful and the lunch was delicious-fresh lobster and coconut rice. Costa Maya was the only 'meh' day. We did the Bacalar Lagoon tour, which was a very long drive. The lagoon is stunning, the 'seven colors of blue' are real, but I spent more time on a bus than I did in the water. If you don't mind long travel times, it's worth it, but if you want to relax, maybe pick something closer to the pier. Overall, a great mix of activities across the three stops. I felt like I got a good taste of both Mexico and Honduras.

review_text: In Roatan we booked a zipline and animal sanctuary combo which ended up being the most memorable part of the trip. The zipline went over thick jungle and then we stopped to see sloths and monkeys up close. The guides were friendly and kept things moving without feeling rushed. Costa Maya was more laid back. We grabbed a taxi to a beach club just outside the main port area and spent the afternoon in the water and under shade. It was not fancy but it was peaceful and easy to enjoy. In Cozumel we walked around the port area first, then took a short ride to a snorkeling spot. The water was clear but currents made it tricky for beginners in our group. I would say Roatan had the best balance of activity and nature, while Costa Maya was best for pure relaxation and Cozumel was somewhere in between.

review_text: For our day in Cozumel, we booked a private catamaran. Best decision ever. We got away from the cruise crowds and had a private reef to ourselves. The crew caught fresh conch and made ceviche right on the boat. It was the highlight of the trip. In Costa Maya, we did the tequila seminar. It was educational, though they really push you to buy the expensive bottles at the end. Roatan was our least favorite. We tried to do a walking tour but it was so hot and the sidewalks were uneven. We ended up just heading back to the ship for a nap. I think next time I'd book a water-based excursion for Roatan since being on land was just too humid for us.

review_text: In Cozumel, we did the bar hop tour to the east side. It was a great way to see the undeveloped parts of the island away from the tourist traps. Our guide was local and had so many stories about the island's history. We didn't do much in Costa Maya, just grabbed a couple of drinks at the port pool. It's a nice facility but very expensive compared to local spots. Roatan was our snorkeling day. The reef there is in much better shape than the ones I've seen in the Virgin Islands. We saw a sea turtle and several stingrays. review_text: Roatan ended up being our favorite stop, mostly because we booked a small-group island tour that included a wildlife sanctuary and a quiet beach on the other side of the island. The drive itself was eye-opening, seeing neighborhoods beyond the cruise port area. Holding a sloth felt surreal, even if it was clearly set up for tourists. The beach portion was relaxed and not overcrowded, which we appreciated.  Costa Maya was more frustrating. We tried to do our own thing and walk beyond the port, but it felt a bit disorganized once outside. We ended up at a beach club that was fine but nothing memorable. Cozumel felt the easiest to navigate. We just grabbed a taxi downtown, wandered shops, and had lunch by the water. It was simple but enjoyable.

review_text: I was really looking forward to the ruins in Costa Maya, but the tour was cancelled due to a mechanical issue with the bus. We were pretty bummed. We ended up just staying in the port area which is basically one big mall. In Cozumel, we did the chocolate tasting and it was actually very educational. I didn't realize how much history goes into it! Roatan was the best for nature. We did a botanical garden walk and saw some amazing birds. I just wish the ports weren't so geared towards selling you plastic trinkets. The natural beauty of Honduras is stunning, but you have to look past the tourist traps to find it. Next time I'd book a private car in Roatan to see the East End where it's supposedly much quieter. Cozumel is still the king of shopping though.

review_text: Roatan ended up being the most memorable stop for us because we booked a small snorkeling excursion that took us out to a calmer reef area. The water visibility was surprisingly good and the guide kept things organized so we weren't rushed. Costa Maya felt more like a controlled shopping area unless you had a pre-booked tour, so we mostly just walked around the port complex there. In Cozumel, we grabbed a taxi into town and wandered the central square and waterfront, which was easy but very crowded with other cruise groups. I'd recommend only using reputable tour companies there because the infrastructure isn't great. The iguana farm was interesting though, hundreds of them just roaming around.

review_text: Roatan felt the most vibrant culturally. Our guide pointed out schools, markets, and different communities, which added context beyond just activities. Costa Maya was more about the excursion itself-we visited ruins and learned about Mayan history, which I appreciated, but the experience felt somewhat scripted. Cozumel was very tourist-forward, but I still enjoyed a beach club where the water was calm and clear. I noticed that Cozumel had the most crowd overlap with other ships, which made certain areas feel congested. Overall, I valued Roatan the most because it felt like we actually saw the island rather than just passing through.

review_text: Roatan was the highlight for us. We booked a private driver named Victor who took us all over the island before the crowds hit the West End. The greenery is stunning, though the traffic near the port at Coxen Hole is absolutely no joke. We spent about three hours at West Bay Beach and the snorkeling right off the shore was some of the best I've seen in the Caribbean. We did find the vendors a bit pushy there, but a polite 'no' usually worked. In Cozumel, we decided to skip the organized excursions and just rented a jeep to drive to the 'wild side' of the island. It was so much better than the crowded pier area. We stopped at Coconuts for a drink and just enjoyed the view of the waves hitting the rocks. The contrast between the two sides of the island is crazy. Definitely felt like we had enough time in both places, but I wish the Costa Maya stop was longer because by the time we got back from the ruins, we had zero time to explore the actual port shops or the pool area.

review_text: Roatan was the highlight for us. We booked a private driver named Victor who took us all over the island before the crowds hit the West End. The greenery is stunning, though the traffic near the port at Coxen Hole is absolutely no joke. We spent about three hours at West Bay Beach and the snorkeling right off the shore was some of the best I've seen in the Caribbean. We did find the vendors a bit pushy there, but a polite 'no' usually worked. In Cozumel, we decided to skip the organized excursions and just rented a jeep to drive to the 'wild side' of the island. It was so much better than the crowded pier area. We stopped at Coconuts for a drink and just enjoyed the view of the waves hitting the rocks. The contrast between the two sides of the island is crazy. Definitely felt like we had enough time in both places, but I wish the Costa Maya stop was longer because by the time we got back from the ruins, we had zero time to explore the actual port shops or the pool area.

review_text: Roatan was our favorite stop on this itinerary. We booked a guided island tour that included a visit to a sloth and monkey sanctuary, a short scenic drive over the hills, and a beach break at the end. The animal encounter was the highlight because the guides explained a lot about conservation and how tourism supports local work. After that we went to a small local beach where the water was calm and clear, and we had about an hour to swim before heading back. Costa Maya felt very different. The port area was built up and easy to navigate, but we chose to leave the immediate shopping zone and take a taxi to a quieter beach club. It was less crowded and we appreciated having space to relax instead of being surrounded by cruise crowds. The ride there was short, maybe fifteen minutes, and the driver pointed out small villages along the way. Cozumel was our most active day. We rented a private driver and did a mix of snorkeling and a quick stop near a beach club area. The snorkeling spot had decent visibility but currents picked up later in the morning so we did not stay long. Overall, I liked how each port offered a different pace: Roatan for nature and animals, Costa Maya for a relaxed beach day, and Cozumel for activity and exploring.

After that we went to a small local beach where the water was calm and clear, and we had about an hour to swim before heading back. Costa Maya felt very different. The port area was built up and easy to navigate, but we chose to leave the immediate shopping zone and take a taxi to a quieter beach club. It was less crowded and we appreciated having space to relax instead of being surrounded by cruise crowds. The ride there was short, maybe fifteen minutes, and the driver pointed out small villages along the way. Cozumel was our most active day. We rented a private driver and did a mix of snorkeling and a quick stop near a beach club area. The snorkeling spot had decent visibility but currents picked up later in the morning so we did not stay long. Overall, I liked how each port offered a different pace: Roatan for nature and animals, Costa Maya for a relaxed beach day, and Cozumel for activity and exploring.

review_text: We loved the history in Costa Maya! The Mayan ruins at Chacchoben are a must-see if you haven't been. Our guide, Ivan, was so passionate and pointed out spider monkeys in the trees above the temples. It felt very Indiana Jones. Cozumel was a bit of a contrast. We did the Jeep tour around the island. The east side of the island is much more rugged and beautiful than the side where the ships dock. No electricity over there, just wild waves and small beach bars. Roatan was our relaxation day. We went to Little French Key. It's a bit pricey to get out there, but the water is calm and the lunch was fantastic-fresh lobster and coconut rice. One thing to note: the pier in Roatan is very long, so be prepared for a walk if you don't use the 'magic chair' lift.

review_text: This itinerary really depends on how much planning you do ahead of time. In Roatan, we booked a private driver instead of a large group excursion, which made a huge difference. We were able to stop at a couple of scenic overlooks, a small beach stretch, and even a local area where it felt like everyday life was still going on outside the tourism zones. That flexibility made Roatan feel the most authentic of the three stops. Costa Maya, however, felt very controlled in comparison. We didn't book an excursion there and ended up staying inside the port complex longer than planned. It was clean and organized, but it didn't feel like we saw anything beyond the immediate cruise area. Cozumel was somewhere in the middle for us. We walked into town and explored a few streets, but the heat and crowds made it less comfortable to linger. Transportation back to the ship was easy, but the overall experience felt more tourist-heavy than immersive. If I were to redo this itinerary, I'd prioritize pre-booking something meaningful in Costa Maya and allow more structured exploration in Roatan, because the contrast between planned and unplanned days really shaped how each port felt.

That flexibility made Roatan feel the most authentic of the three stops. Costa Maya, however, felt very controlled in comparison. We didn't book an excursion there and ended up staying inside the port complex longer than planned. It was clean and organized, but it didn't feel like we saw anything beyond the immediate cruise area. Cozumel was somewhere in the middle for us. We walked into town and explored a few streets, but the heat and crowds made it less comfortable to linger. Transportation back to the ship was easy, but the overall experience felt more tourist-heavy than immersive. If I were to redo this itinerary, I'd prioritize pre-booking something meaningful in Costa Maya and allow more structured exploration in Roatan, because the contrast between planned and unplanned days really shaped how each port felt.

Cozumel we booked a snorkeling excursion that had good visibility but felt slightly rushed due to multiple stops and other boats around. Still, we saw a lot of marine life and enjoyed the day overall.

review_text: Our trip to the Chacchoben ruins from Costa Maya was incredible. Our guide, Ivan, was so knowledgeable about Mayan history and made the long bus ride fly by with stories. The ruins themselves are breathtaking, especially since you can still see where the jungle is reclaiming some of the structures. It was a bit hot and humid, so bring plenty of water. In Cozumel, we did a chocolate making workshop which was fun for the kids, but I felt it was a bit overpriced for what it was. We skipped Roatan entirely because the weather looked shaky and we wanted to enjoy the quiet ship.

review_text: I really enjoyed the history at Chacchoben in Costa Maya. Our guide was actually of Mayan descent and told us stories passed down through his family. It's a long day though, especially with the bus ride. Cozumel is just too crowded for me these days. Every time I go, there are more people and more vendors yelling at you to buy t-shirts. Roatan is still the gem of this itinerary. The greenery and the hills are beautiful as you sail in. We did a catamaran sail there that was very peaceful.

If you like structure, it's fine, but spontaneous travelers might find it frustrating.

review_text: This itinerary gave a good mix, but I think your experience depends heavily on what you book. In Roatan, we chose a smaller, locally run tour and it made all the difference. The guide shared personal stories and took us to less crowded spots. Costa Maya felt more generic, even though the ruins themselves were impressive. The logistics there-long bus rides, early departures-made the day feel tiring. Cozumel was the easiest to navigate and had the most options, but also the most people. If I had to rank them, Roatan first for authenticity, Cozumel second for convenience, and Costa Maya last due to the effort required.

review_text: Roatan was incredible but the logistics were a bit of a headache. We booked the shipwreck snorkel and while the reef was pristine, the bus drive from the pier took nearly an hour due to some local construction. It felt like we only got 45 minutes in the water before we had to dry off and head back. Cozumel was a much smoother experience; we just walked off the boat and grabbed a taxi to the town square. Had some of the best street tacos of my life and did a bit of silver shopping. Costa Maya was purely a beach day for us at the port pool. It's convenient if you don't want to deal with the hassle of excursions, but it definitely feels more like a theme park than a destination. I wish we had more time in Roatan to actually see the island instead of just sitting in traffic.

review_text: The ports were a mixed bag. I loved the history in Costa Maya-the ruins are a must-see even if the drive is long. Roatan was stunning but we had a bad experience with a local taxi driver who tried to overcharge us at the end of the day. It left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth. Cozumel was the most professional; everything is streamlined for tourists. We did the submarine tour and it was fascinating to see the reef from 100 feet down. I think the itinerary is good, but you have to be careful in Roatan if you aren't on an official ship excursion. The time spent in each port was mostly okay, but we felt very rushed in Costa Maya because the ruins tour takes up almost the whole window. I'd love an extra two hours there just to relax after the long bus ride back.

review_text: Cozumel is always a favorite. We went to Mr. Sanchos for the day. It's an all-inclusive beach club and they really take care of you. The food was surprisingly good for a buffet and the drinks kept coming. It was very crowded though, so if you want peace and quiet, this isn't it. Roatan was beautiful but the pier at Coxen Hole is very industrial looking. We did a catamaran snorkel trip and saw some great coral. The crew was fun but the equipment was a bit dated. Costa Maya was our last stop. We just walked the pier and did some souvenir shopping. The walk from the ship to the actual port exit is very long, especially in the heat, so take the little tram if it's running. Overall, a solid itinerary but I felt like the port times were a little short for Roatan.

Roatan was beautiful but the pier at Coxen Hole is very industrial looking. We did a catamaran snorkel trip and saw some great coral. The crew was fun but the equipment was a bit dated. Costa Maya was our last stop. We just walked the pier and did some souvenir shopping. The walk from the ship to the actual port exit is very long, especially in the heat, so take the little tram if it's running. Overall, a solid itinerary but I felt like the port times were a little short for Roatan.

review_text: I struggled with the walking in Costa Maya. The pier is huge and the shuttle was full. Once in the port, it's all cobblestones which was hard for my walker. Cozumel was much more accessible. We took a van to the dolphin encounter and it was very well managed for people with mobility issues. Roatan was a bit of a challenge too, very hilly. We stayed in the port area and looked at the shops. The crafts in Roatan were much more unique than the stuff in Mexico-lots of beautiful wood carvings. I wish the cruise line provided more information about the walking distances at each pier before we got off.

review_text: Did the Chacchoben ruins in Costa Maya. The bus ride was nearly an hour each way but the guide was so knowledgeable about Mayan history that the time flew by. Seeing the pyramids poking through the jungle canopy was breathtaking. Just be prepared for the humidity! We also did a catamaran snorkel in Cozumel. The reef was okay, but I've seen better in other parts of the Caribbean. The crew made the trip fun with music and drinks on the way back, though. Roatan felt a bit rushed; our ship cleared customs late so we only had about four hours on the island, which wasn't enough to really see anything beyond the immediate port area and a quick lunch. I'd recommend prioritizing the ruins if you haven't seen them.

We just sat by the port pool which is actually very nice and free to use. The only thing is the drinks there are ship prices, not Mexico prices. It was a good mix of ports, though I wish there was more of a cultural focus in the ship-sponsored tours rather than just beach clubs.

review_text: This was my third time on this itinerary. Roatan continues to be my favorite. The lush green mountains meeting the blue water is just unbeatable. We did a fishing charter this time and caught some snapper that a local place cooked up for us. Costa Maya hasn't changed much-still a tourist trap at the pier, but Mahahual is slowly getting more developed. The seaweed problem in Costa Maya seems to be getting worse every year though. Cozumel is always reliable. We did the salsa and salsa tour (making salsa and dancing salsa). It's cheesy but a lot of fun with a group of friends. The port logistics were smooth at all three stops, though the security line to get back on the ship in Cozumel was nearly 30 minutes long in the direct sun. Overall, a great trip for anyone who loves the sun, but I'd suggest more time in Roatan and less in Costa Maya if they ever change the schedule.

We did the shore excursion to the lagoon, but it was so crowded we couldn't find a lounge chair. Roatan was better; we went to a small resort called Turquoise Bay. It was quiet and the water was like glass. The only issue was the long drive across the island, which took about 45 minutes each way.

review_text: Roatan offered the most memorable experience for me. We joined a small group excursion that combined a wildlife visit and a beach stop, and it felt well paced without being rushed. Costa Maya was a bit disappointing because we didn't book anything in advance and ended up staying within the port complex, which felt artificial. Cozumel redeemed things slightly. We found a quieter beach farther from the main dock area, but it required negotiating with taxi drivers and figuring out timing to get back. Overall, I'd say planning ahead is essential for these ports.

review_text: I loved the variety on this trip! Roatan had the best nature-the chocolate factory tour was so cool and the jungle smells amazing after it rains. Costa Maya was our beach day; we just sat under a palapa in Mahahual and watched the waves. It was very relaxing, though the seaweed was a bit thick in some spots. Cozumel was our big excursion day where we went to the San Gervasio ruins. They aren't as big as the ones on the mainland, but they were very peaceful and not nearly as crowded. I felt like we had plenty of time in each port, though I wish Cozumel stayed open a bit later into the evening so we could have had dinner on land. The transition from the ship to the shore was easy at all three stops, which isn't always the case. Definitely a solid itinerary for people who like a mix of history and relaxation.

review_text: Traveling with three kids is hard but these ports made it easy. Roatan's monkey park was the biggest hit. The kids are still talking about the monkeys jumping on their heads. Costa Maya was the only place I felt slightly unsure about where to go after leaving the port area. I ended up just staying within the complex, which was fine but not very memorable.

review_text: Cozumel is a diver's paradise. I did a two-tank dive at Palancar Reef and the visibility was stunning, easily 100 feet. The coral formations are huge. My husband stayed on the ship that day but joined me in Roatan for the beach. Roatan has a lot of charm but the local infrastructure is clearly struggling with the amount of tourists. Costa Maya was just a shopping day for us. We found some nice silver jewelry in one of the shops near the back of the port, though you have to haggle quite a bit to get a fair price. Overall a good mix of ports.

Cozumel felt a bit 'tired'-the same shops and the same tours I saw five years ago. Costa Maya is growing fast, but the infrastructure isn't quite there. The line for taxis back to the port was nearly 40 minutes long in the blazing sun. They need more organization for the independent travelers. Still, the beach at Mahahual is beautiful if you find a spot without the sea grass.

The line for taxis back to the port was nearly 40 minutes long in the blazing sun. They need more organization for the independent travelers. Still, the beach at Mahahual is beautiful if you find a spot without the sea grass.

review_text: Cozumel is the gold standard for port organization. Everything flows so well. We did a chocolate and wine tasting which was very sophisticated and tasty. Costa Maya is the opposite. It feels like you're being funneled through a maze of shops just to leave the port area. It's annoying. We eventually made it out to a small restaurant in Mahahual called Nohoch Kay for amazing fish tacos. Roatan's natural beauty is the best of the three, but the infrastructure is lacking. We went to the botanical gardens and it was lovely, but the path was very muddy and slippery. Definitely wear good shoes if you go off the beaten path in Roatan. The itinerary overall was great for seeing different sides of the Western Caribbean.

Costa Maya was our 'ship day'-we looked at the crowds on the pier and decided to just stay on board and enjoy the quiet pool. review_text: Cozumel was the highlight for our group. We bypassed the standard cruise excursions and took a taxi to Punta Sur Eco Beach Park. It's about a 35-minute drive from the pier, but absolutely worth it for the lighthouse views and the crocodile spotting in the lagoon. The beach there is much quieter than the clubs closer to the ship. Roatan was also beautiful, but the pier area in Coxen Hole felt a bit chaotic with everyone trying to sell you a taxi ride. We eventually made it to West Bay for some snorkeling, which was world-class, though we felt a bit rushed to get back before the ship departed. Costa Maya was our 'stay on the ship' day. We walked around the port area for twenty minutes, but it felt like a giant, overpriced shopping mall designed just for tourists. If you aren't doing a long bus ride to the ruins, there isn't much substance right at the dock. We preferred the quiet pool on the ship instead.
sentence_text: Cozumel was the highlight for our group.

review_text: Costa Maya ruins are a must-see! Chaccoben is amazing. The jungle setting makes you feel like Indiana Jones. The guides are very respectful of the history. Cozumel is better for water sports. We did a helmet dive which was a unique way to see the reef without needing to know how to scuba. Roatan was a bit of a mixed bag. The scenery is 10/10 but the infrastructure is struggling. We were stuck in a shuttle for 45 minutes just trying to get out of the port area. Once we got to our destination it was fine, but the logistics on that island need work.

review_text: We traveled with three kids and these ports were perfect for them. In Cozumel, we did the sea lion encounter at Chankanaab and they haven't stopped talking about it. The park is very well maintained. In Roatan, we did a beach day at a resort that had a big inflatable water park in the ocean. It kept them busy for hours. Costa Maya was actually quite fun for the kids too because of the big pool right in the middle of the port area. It's shallow and safe. My only complaint is the cost of food in the ports. A simple lunch for five people in Cozumel cost us nearly $120. Next time we might just head back to the ship for lunch before going back out. The port times were generous enough that we could have done that if we had planned better.

review_text: Wasn't a fan of the Costa Maya port. It's basically a maze of souvenir shops that you have to walk through to get anywhere. We ended up just taking a quick taxi to Mahahual for some street tacos which were excellent, but the beach there had a lot of seaweed when we visited. Cozumel was a much smoother experience. We did the America's Cup 12-meter regatta excursion and it was exhilarating to actually help sail those boats. Roatan was nice but very humid. We did a glass-bottom boat tour because my wife doesn't like to swim, and we still saw plenty of coral and fish. The pier in Roatan is quite long, so be prepared for a bit of a hike if you aren't using the chairlift thing they have there.

review_text: I'm a bit of a history buff, so I was looking forward to the ruins. Chacchoben in Costa Maya didn't disappoint. The climbable sections are limited now to preserve them, but the scale is still impressive. Cozumel felt too commercialized for me. It's basically one giant pharmacy and jewelry store after another. We took a ferry to Playa del Carmen but the crossing was very rough-lots of seasick passengers. Roatan was the most authentic-feeling stop. We visited a local school as part of a 'giving back' excursion. It was humbling and much better than sitting on a beach. The logistics in Roatan were a bit messy with the bus dispatch, but the experience itself was the highlight of my cruise. Wish we had stayed later in Mexico to see the sunset.

The climbable sections are limited now to preserve them, but the scale is still impressive. Cozumel felt too commercialized for me. It's basically one giant pharmacy and jewelry store after another. We took a ferry to Playa del Carmen but the crossing was very rough-lots of seasick passengers. Roatan was the most authentic-feeling stop. We visited a local school as part of a 'giving back' excursion. It was humbling and much better than sitting on a beach. The logistics in Roatan were a bit messy with the bus dispatch, but the experience itself was the highlight of my cruise. Wish we had stayed later in Mexico to see the sunset.

Cozumel was too commercial for me. It felt like every square inch was designed to sell me a t-shirt or a diamond ring. Roatan was better, but the pier at Coxen Hole is very cramped and chaotic. We did the sloth encounter which was cute, but the tour felt a bit like an assembly line moving people through as fast as possible. I would have liked more time to just sit and enjoy the jungle.

review_text: I've done a similar itinerary before and this one felt pretty typical. Roatan stood out again because we hired a private driver who took us to less crowded areas, including a quiet beach and a small local restaurant. Costa Maya felt very geared toward tourists. Even outside the port, it didn't feel like we were seeing much beyond what was set up for visitors. Cozumel had the most options, but also the most congestion. We did a snorkeling trip there and it felt a bit like a production line. Overall, Roatan felt the most authentic, while the other two required more effort to find something that didn't feel overly commercial.

Costa Maya was a bit of a bore for us, we just did some souvenir shopping and went back on. I think I would skip Costa Maya next time or book a much longer tour to see something unique.

review_text: I went into this cruise mostly interested in cultural experiences, and the ports delivered that unevenly but still memorably. Roatan exceeded expectations because we booked a small-group excursion that included a visit to a local community, a short jungle walk, and time near the water. It felt immersive without being overwhelming. Costa Maya was more complicated. The ruins were fascinating and visually striking, but the long transportation time made the day feel dominated by logistics rather than exploration. Cozumel, while more commercial, offered flexibility. We opted out of excursions and created our own plan, which worked well but required some research beforehand. I noticed that crowd levels significantly impacted enjoyment, especially in Cozumel where multiple ships were docked. Overall, I appreciated the variety, but planning ahead was key to getting the most out of each stop.

Roatan was okay, but we found the port area quite confusing to navigate and the excursion we had booked was cancelled at the last minute, so we just ended up walking around the local shops which wasn't very exciting.

review_text: Cozumel is always a favorite for our family. We headed straight to Paradise Beach. It's $68 for the all-inclusive pass now, which felt a bit steep, but the service was top-notch and the kids loved the inflatable water park. The taxi ride was easy and only cost about $16 for the four of us. Roatan was beautiful but the traffic is getting out of hand. It took us nearly 45 minutes to get back from the monkey sanctuary, and we were starting to get nervous about the all-aboard time. Costa Maya was okay, but the walk from the ship to the actual port exit is incredibly long, especially in that humidity. We mostly just did some light shopping for silver and vanilla before heading back. Not a bad trip, but I wish we had more time in Roatan to actually see the island instead of just sitting in a van.

review_text: Avoid the 'all-inclusive' beach breaks in Cozumel if you want a quiet day. We went to one that was wall-to-wall people and the music was so loud we couldn't even talk. It felt like a spring break party. On the other hand, Roatan was very peaceful. We hired a private driver named Ronny who took us all over the island, including some local spots away from the tourists. He took us to a small hilltop restaurant with a view of the whole harbor. Costa Maya was okay, but the port feels very fake. It's basically a maze designed to make you walk past every single shop before you can reach the exit to the street.

review_text: I'm a solo traveler and I felt very safe in all three ports. In Roatan, I joined a group tour for the glass-bottom boat. The reef is spectacular and you don't even have to get wet. Cozumel was easy to navigate on foot, I just spent the afternoon at the museum and then had some coffee at a local cafe. Costa Maya was the only place I felt a bit uneasy because the taxi drivers are very aggressive when you walk out of the port gates. I ended up just going back inside the port area and sitting by the pool. The scheduling was decent, though we arrived in Cozumel very early (7:00 AM) and nothing was open yet. It would be better if we arrived a bit later and stayed into the evening so we could see the nightlife.

review_text: I was really looking forward to Roatan but the weather didn't cooperate. It rained most of the morning so our ziplining excursion was canceled. We ended up just taking a taxi to a chocolate factory which was okay, but a bit of a 'tourist trap' feel. Cozumel saved the trip though! We rented a Jeep and drove to the other side of the island. It's completely undeveloped and rugged-no electricity, just small bars on the beach. It felt like a totally different world compared to the busy cruise terminal. We found a small spot called Coconuts on a cliff and the view was breathtaking. Costa Maya was fine, we just did the pool at the port which was free and actually quite nice. I liked that I could see the ship while I was swimming. Just watch out for the drink prices at the port bars, they are higher than on the ship!

review_text: Cozumel was the absolute highlight for our group. We bypassed the typical ship excursions and booked a private Jeep tour that took us to the 'wild side' of the island. There's no electricity on that side, just these incredible rugged beaches and small bars like Coconuts. It felt like a completely different world compared to the crowded pier. Roatan was also great; we did the zip-lining through the jungle. The views from the top were breathtaking, though the bus ride to the site was a bit bumpy and the local traffic is definitely a concern if you're on a tight schedule. We skipped Costa Maya entirely and stayed on the ship to enjoy the quiet decks. From what we heard from others, the port area there is just a big shopping mall anyway, so I don't feel like we missed much. Overall, the time in Cozumel felt perfect, but I wish we had an extra hour in Roatan to see the west end beaches properly.

review_text: We approached each port differently and that made a big difference. In Cozumel, we booked a smaller beach club that limited capacity, which helped avoid the crowds. Roatan was more of a guided experience for us, with a mix of sightseeing and water activities. Costa Maya was the most difficult to navigate independently. Transportation outside the port wasn't as straightforward, and I wish we had arranged something in advance. The ruins were interesting, but the time spent traveling there reduced the overall enjoyment. I would say Roatan felt the most balanced, Cozumel the most convenient, and Costa Maya required the most effort to enjoy.

Transportation outside the port wasn't as straightforward, and I wish we had arranged something in advance. The ruins were interesting, but the time spent traveling there reduced the overall enjoyment. I would say Roatan felt the most balanced, Cozumel the most convenient, and Costa Maya required the most effort to enjoy.

review_text: We are experienced cruisers so we usually skip the big bus tours. In Cozumel, we rented a car for the day. It's very easy to navigate the island as it's basically one big loop. We found a secluded beach on the east side and had it all to ourselves for two hours. Just watch out for the moped renters; they drive a bit crazy. In Costa Maya, we actually stayed in the port and used the pool. It was crowded but convenient since we didn't want to deal with a long day. Roatan was a bit of a struggle. We tried to do a walking tour but the hills are very steep and there aren't many sidewalks once you leave the immediate port area. We ended up just grabbing a taxi back. If you go to Roatan, definitely plan for transportation. Don't think you can just wander around on foot like you can in some parts of Cozumel. The port schedule was okay, but I wish we had stayed later in Cozumel to see the sunset from the shore.

review_text: I tend to prefer cultural and historical experiences, so I had mixed feelings about this itinerary. Roatan surprised me because we booked a small group tour that included a visit to a local area and a short nature walk, which felt more immersive than expected. Costa Maya was probably the most educational stop because of the ruins, but the logistics made it tiring. The early departure and long drive took away from the overall experience, even though the site itself was impressive. Cozumel was the most flexible port, and we chose to explore on our own instead of booking anything. That worked well, but it did require some planning ahead to avoid the most crowded areas. I think this itinerary works best if you're intentional about what you book at each stop.

review_text: Costa Maya was a struggle with the kids. The walk from the ship to the taxis is long and there's not much shade. Once we got to the water park it was fine, but getting there was stressful. Cozumel was much easier. We did the glass-bottom boat and it kept the little ones entertained without them having to get in the water. Roatan was the highlight for the teens; they did the zipline and said it was the scariest and coolest thing they've ever done. I liked the chocolate factory there. It's a good itinerary for families but be prepared for a lot of walking in the heat. Make sure to bring plenty of small bills for tips and taxis in Mexico, as they aren't great about making change for twenty-dollar bills. Roatan accepted US dollars everywhere we went.

review_text: Each port had its pros and cons, but the biggest factor for me was how time was managed. In Roatan, we booked a nature-focused excursion that included a guided walk through a forested area and a short beach stop. It was memorable, but we were constantly aware of the clock, which made it hard to fully relax. Costa Maya required a longer commitment; we chose to visit nearby ruins, which meant an early departure and a fairly long bus ride. The site itself was impressive, but I would have preferred either more time there or a shorter travel distance. Cozumel felt like a reset-we intentionally avoided excursions and just explored at our own pace. That ended up being the most relaxing day. If anything, I'd say this itinerary works best if you mix structured excursions with at least one completely open day.

review_text: For those visiting Roatan, the monkeys are very clever, so watch your pockets! We had a wonderful day at the Gumbalimba Park. It was very well organized. In Cozumel, we participated in a turtle salvage program which was very educational. It was moving to see the conservation efforts. Costa Maya was our last stop. We found the port area to be very loud with music, which made it hard to relax. We walked further out to find a quiet spot on the beach. The sand is very white and beautiful, but there is a lot of coral rubble, so water shoes are a good idea. Overall, a good variety of islands, though the time spent in each felt a little rushed due to the ship's schedule. I would have liked to stay in Cozumel until sunset.

review_text: I'm a solo traveler and I found Roatan very easy to navigate. I just walked off and found a local driver who took me to West End for $20. Spent the day at a small cafe on the water and did some great shore snorkeling. Cozumel was a bit much for me alone-everyone is trying to pull you into their shop or bar. I ended up going back to the ship after an hour. Costa Maya was actually quite chill if you stay at the very end of the beach away from the cruise pier. The food at the local stalls in Mahahual was much better and cheaper than the port food. I think the time in each port was adequate, though Cozumel feels like it needs a full 12 hours if you want to do the mainland excursions to Tulum.
